findings.statement: 16 MB seals lift ingest-to-routed by at least 1.2x over 64 MB
findings.detail: 16 MB 469044 ops/s against 64 MB 450744 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.041, p=0.0947) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB 463951 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.029, p=0.4034) -- within noise, not a result). Phases at 16 against 64 MB: commit 0.012s/0.013s, seal 0.012s/0.012s, merge 0.011s/0.012s; the loop alone 0.020s/0.021s. Smaller seals move the merges off the drain and onto the other cores while the load runs

findings.statement: at 16 MB seals, device bytes are at most 2.0x the 64 MB arm's
findings.detail: device bytes 10.0 MB at 16 MB seals against 10.0 at 64 MB (1.000x); 32 MB 10.0, 8 MB 10.0. Disk after the drain 3.7/3.7/3.7/3.7 MB for 64/32/16/8, partitions 1/1/1/1. Every merge round rewrites the live set the new pieces touch; this is that amplification, measured

findings.statement: reads after the drain do not differ across seal sizes
findings.detail: 164 ns per point read at 64 MB, 164 at 32, 160 at 16 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.985, p=0.3785) -- within noise, not a result), 163 at 8 (8mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.006, p=0.8102) -- within noise, not a result). After the drain every arm is partitions only and the partition count is set by max_keys, not the seal size

findings.statement: the sweep has an interior optimum: 8 MB seals ingest no faster than 16 MB
findings.detail: 8 MB 478546 ops/s against 16 MB 469044 (8mb vs 16mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.020, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result); device bytes 10.0 against 10.0 MB, merge phase 0.011s against 0.011s. Below some size the merge amplification and the per-seal fixed costs take back what the overlap gave

findings.statement: 32 MB seals over 64 MB partitions ingest at least 1.10x the 64 MB arm
findings.detail: 32mb-p64 462721 ops/s against 64 MB 450744 (32mb-p64 vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.027, p=0.5309) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB with coupled partitions 463951 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.029, p=0.4034) -- within noise, not a result). Phases 32mb-p64 against 64 MB: commit 0.014s/0.013s, seal 0.012s/0.012s, merge 0.011s/0.012s; device bytes 10.0 against 10.0 MB; partitions 1 against 1. Three seals overlap the load where one did, and no extra merge round is triggered

findings.statement: 32 MB seals over 64 MB partitions read no slower than 64 MB seals after the drain
findings.detail: 165 ns per point read for 32mb-p64 against 164 at 64 MB (32mb-p64 vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.023, p=0.9362) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB with coupled partitions 164 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.017, p=0.6889) -- within noise, not a result). Same partition count, same reads; the read cost the first run charged to the seal size was the partition count's

notes: four arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, one option apart: seal_bytes 64 MB (shipping), 32, 16 and 8, on f49's shape -- the f42 durable load with the drain (seal, join, partition) inside the timed window. Smaller seals move merges off the drain and onto the other cores while the load runs; the price is every merge round rewriting the live set.
